editorial:
When their mum dies suddenly, two brothers are left to figure out life on their own. Danny dives into music, sex, and drugs, while younger Jack builds a strange comfort by turning a life-size mannequin into a stand-in mum. It sounds odd, but the movie plays it with real heart and sadness. You watch two kids handle grief in very different ways, and that contrast gives the story its pull. The tone mixes awkward laughs with heavy moments, so you never quite know whether to smile or ache. It feels intimate and raw, like peeking into a family that has lost its center.

The acting carries a lot here, especially the brothers' chemistry and the way Jack treats the mannequin like a real person. Pacing is steady, not rushed, letting small moments land. Pros: emotional honesty, unique premise, strong sibling tension. Cons: some scenes feel uncomfortable, and the drug side can be bleak. If you like coming-of-age dramas with a strange edge, this is for you. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Jack's bond with the mannequin reaches a breaking point as Danny finally sees how far his brother has gone to avoid grief. Instead of staying stuck in denial, Jack lets go of the fake mum and faces the loss with Danny beside him. The movie ends on a quiet, hopeful note, suggesting the brothers may finally start healing together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional family dramas with an unusual twist.
